name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,170

clue.text: Alter past ethos as quickly as possible

indicators.note: to alter something is to change it, so the letters that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: the two words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A call to change an old outlook in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alter' reads as a command aimed at the ethos, but it only signals rearranging the nine letters of the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Posthaste is an old adverb meaning with all speed, from the urgent pace of riders carrying the mail.

clue.text: Model right to abandon writing

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so a letter drops out of the word

blocks.note: prose is ordinary written language
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A fashion model gives up a writing career for the right reasons.
explanation.walkthrough: PROSE loses its R to leave POSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are verbs describing someone holding a position for an artist or photographer.

clue.text: Dog’s range that is large

blocks.note: a span is an extent or range
i.e. is the abbreviation of Latin id est, that is
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A big dog roams over a wide territory.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay rather than marking possession.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaniel is a breed of gun dog with long drooping ears, an example of the general class.

clue.text: Dwelling — haunt on regular basis

indicators.note: something done on a regular basis happens at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: first, third and fifth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A cabin where someone hangs out routinely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haunt' looks like a synonym of dwelling, but it only supplies its odd letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A hut is a small simple shelter, a humble kind of home or abode.

clue.text: Put street on list for walk

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it, so it comes first

blocks.note: St is the address abbreviation for street
a roll is a list of names, as in a roll call

explanation.surface: Someone adds a street to a list of walking routes.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'on' means the first piece sits above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroll is a leisurely walk, a direct synonym for an unhurried amble.

clue.text: Inspire group of followers giving up time for Conservative

indicators.note: giving up one thing for another means swapping, so one letter is replaced by a different one

blocks.note: an entourage is the retinue that follows an important person
T is the abbreviation for time
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A political leader motivates supporters who abandon their time for the Conservative party.
explanation.walkthrough: The T of ENTOURAGE is swapped for C.
explanation.definitionFit: To encourage someone is to give them confidence or spirit, which is what inspiring them does.

clue.text: Dad’s attempt

blocks.note: first meaning: an informal word for father
second meaning: a try

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s reads as possession but stands for 'is', linking two meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a familiar name for father and a colloquial noun for a try at something.

clue.text: Jacket of expected standard, okay essentially

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so only the central letters are kept

blocks.note: par is the expected or normal level, as in golf
the two central letters of the word

explanation.surface: A coat judged to be of decent, acceptable quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essentially' sounds like 'basically' in the surface, but it takes the heart of the word it follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded windproof jacket, an example of outerwear.

clue.text: Spacecraft, one in landing place

indicators.note: a thing that is in another sits inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: a pier is where boats land passengers
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spacecraft sits at its landing site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Landing place' suggests a launchpad or spaceport, but it is a jetty for boats. Pioneer was a series of NASA space probes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pioneer 10 and 11 were NASA probes sent past Jupiter and Saturn, a named example of a spacecraft.

clue.text: Broadcast frightens cat terribly? Just a bit

indicators.note: only a bit of the phrase is wanted, a run of letters lying inside it

blocks.note: the run spans the end of the first word, the whole second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A radio programme scares a cat badly, though only slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' looks like radio, but here it is the old farming verb for sowing seed widely.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast seed is to sow it by hand over a wide area, which is to strew it about.

clue.text: Load vehicle and leave

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Pack up the van and drive off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Load' reads as an instruction, but it is the noun defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is the goods carried by a ship, plane or lorry, the freight it holds.

clue.text: Make two and two five? Call it ace sum bizarrely!

indicators.note: something done bizarrely is done in a strange, disordered way, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the four words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone gets the arithmetic wrong and calls the result a great sum.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase describing a sum gone wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting five from two plus two is a playful example of an arithmetic error or wrong reckoning.

clue.text: Agreement population count must include only necessary statistics at first

indicators.note: what comes at first is at the front, so each word gives its opening letter
to include something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a census is an official count of a population
the opening letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A deal about a census: it should only contain the essential figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Population count' reads as part of the surface story but is the official survey word; 'must include' places the initials inside it after its opening C.
explanation.definitionFit: A consensus is a general accord reached by a group, a synonym for shared agreement.

clue.text: Regretting welcoming learner’s decision

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: to rue is to regret
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Someone regrets having let a student make the call.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s on 'learner' stands for 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruling is an official judgement handed down by a judge or referee, a synonym for decision.

clue.text: Seeking major changes in type of tyre, costs initially to be absorbed

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is taken
something absorbed is soaked up inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a radial is a tyre with cords running across the tread
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A garage wants to overhaul its tyre range while swallowing the costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seeking major changes' is an adjective phrase; radical reformers want sweeping change.
explanation.definitionFit: In politics a radical favours thorough or fundamental reform rather than gradual adjustment.

clue.text: Smart agent writing paper after returning

indicators.note: what comes after follows, so the second piece is placed behind the first
to return is to go back the way you came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a rep is a sales agent or representative
a pad is a block of writing paper

explanation.surface: A well-dressed salesman comes back carrying his stationery.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole of REPPAD is reversed, not just the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart in the sense of neat and stylishly dressed, which is what dapper describes in a man.

clue.text: Accurate summary, English

blocks.note: a précis is a short summary of a text
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A faithful summary written for an English class.
explanation.walkthrough: The accent on précis is dropped in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Precise and accurate are synonyms, both meaning exact and free from error.

clue.text: Oil country, they say

indicators.note: what people say is spoken, so the word is matched by its sound

blocks.note: Greece is a country in southern Europe

explanation.surface: People call a certain nation an oil producer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil country' suggests a petrostate, but the country is a Mediterranean one heard as a lubricant.
explanation.definitionFit: To grease a hinge is to lubricate it, the same as to oil it; both work as noun or verb.

clue.text: Down, need this read — novel

indicators.note: something novel is new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the three words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Feeling low, someone wants a novel to read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book to read, but it is the adjective new, signalling rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down is being low in spirits, and disheartened means having lost hope or confidence.

clue.text: Informed about Left’s colloquial talk

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: in underworld speech to sing is to tell tales to the police
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: An informer reports on the political Left's casual chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Informed' means told the police, as a grass sings; the apostrophe-s stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is very informal vocabulary used in conversation rather than in formal writing.

clue.text: Take notice of which three were ahead in the end

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that letter is kept from each

blocks.note: final letter of the word
final letter of the word
final letter of the word
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Pay attention to which three runners led at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a race result; only the tails of four words matter.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed a warning is to pay attention to it, a verb synonym for noticing and acting on it.

clue.text: Confusion as cash out of order with nothing being accepted

indicators.note: what is accepted is taken in, so one piece goes inside the other
things out of order are jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A cash machine is broken and takes in nothing, causing bedlam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of order' suggests a broken machine, but it signals rearranging the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaos is complete disorder, and confusion in this sense means a state of turmoil.

clue.text: Most important I have place for keeping documents

blocks.note: arch means chief, as in archenemy
the contraction I've

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of owning a vital records store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most important' is the prefix sense of arch, as in arch-rival.
explanation.definitionFit: An archive is a repository where historical records and papers are stored.

clue.text: Copper right — it is an unfriendly beast

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A police officer is correct that the animal is hostile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman, but it is the metal by its chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A cur is a snappish, aggressive mongrel dog, an animal that is hostile to people.

clue.text: Part of tree record

blocks.note: first meaning: a section cut from a trunk or branch
second meaning: an official written record, as of a voyage

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like tree rings recording age; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a chunk of felled timber and a ship's or diary-style register of events.

clue.text: Leader in parade, he’s getting excited

indicators.note: something excited is agitated and stirred up, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: The man at the front of a procession is thrilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader in parade' seems one definition, but 'parade' belongs to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A spearhead is the person or group at the forefront of a campaign or attack, leading it.
